differentiable.def: A function is differentiable at $x = a$ when $f'(a) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(a + h) - f(a)}{h}$ exists as a finite number, and differentiable on an interval when it is differentiable at every point of it. Differentiable implies continuous; the converse is false.

corner.def: A point where a continuous graph has no derivative: a corner (the left and right slopes are different numbers, as for $|x|$ at 0), a cusp (the slopes grow without bound in opposite directions, as for $x^{2/3}$ at 0) or a vertical tangent line (as for $\sqrt[3]{x}$ at 0).
